content.comment_body: Hello, I would like to know how you configured PUT communication from [product_name] to [product_name]. I can perform GET operations and read data from [product_name] without issues, but PUT does not work for me. I require both PUT and GET on [product_name], with [product_name] set as the server, because I want to trigger communication periodically by using a REQUEST input with the PUT function block. I have attached my configuration as a .zip file. Thanks for your assistance.

Hello [user_name], On the German forum, I provided an example for communication between [product_name] and [product_name]. In this setup, [product_name] acts as the client and [product_name] is the server. You may find this example useful. The S7 project and project are attached, but please note the description is only available in German.
Thank you, your input was very helpful.
Has your problem been solved now?

Here's an example where [product_name] is the client and [product_name] serves as the server. Under protection settings, you must enable 'Access via PUT/GET communication through remote partners.' You don't need the PUT/GET function blocks for this, but the active connection should be deselected in 'Special connection properties.' When [product_name] is the client, data exchange is simpler compared to PUT/GET communication using extra function blocks and data blocks.

Thank you. I've resolved my issue with the PUT function block. We previously configured [product_name] as the client and now want to test reversed communication because our connection occasionally drops. Multiple [product_name] units are linked to a single [product_name] in our setup. It seems that frequent cyclic communication from [product_name] to [product_name] causes the connection to crash momentarily; we measured this using Wireshark. By using active connection establishment with PUT/GET blocks on [product_name], we can trigger communication requests only when needed.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants addressed configuration issues and reliability concerns regarding PUT/GET communication between different [product_name] devices. While GET (read) operations function normally, PUT (write) communications can be unstable, especially in projects with multiple [product_name] units acting as clients. Solutions focused on specific configuration settings and flexible role assignment, emphasizing the importance of establishing communications only when needed for enhanced stability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect robust and easily configurable PUT/GET communication between their [product_name] devices, seeking the ability to trigger data transfers as required to improve overall system reliability and performance.
